harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a fresh 3-node MariaDB Galera cluster (10.11.18) across node1/node2/node3 on CentOS Stream 10, took it fully down for a simulated maintenance window, brought it back with all committed writes intact, then individually restarted (native reboot) each node one at a time and verified changed boot identity plus post-reboot cluster health/data on all three.
actions_performed: Installed mariadb-server, mariadb-server-galera, galera packages on node1, node2, node3
Opened firewalld ports 3306, 4567/tcp+udp, 4568, 4444 on all nodes

Configured /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf with wsrep cluster address, per-node identity, and rsync SST (mariabackup SST failed due to an SELinux connectto denial on mysqld_t; switched to rsync to avoid that gap)
Generated sst and appuser DB credentials on node1 itself via openssl rand, distributed the sst password to node2/node3 over the cluster SSH key
Bootstrapped Galera on node1 (galera_new_cluster), joined node2 and node3, reaching cluster size 3, all Synced
Created appdb.orders table with committed rows as the application data baseline, verified replication to all 3 nodes

Performed full maintenance-window shutdown: stopped mariadb on node3, node2, then node1 (last-stopped retained highest seqno / safe_to_bootstrap:1), confirmed all three fully inactive with no mariadbd processes running

Recovered cluster: bootstrapped node1, started node2 and node3, confirmed cluster size 3 all Synced and all committed rows present on every node; verified writes/reads work from a non-bootstrap node (node2) and replicate everywhere
Captured baseline boot_id on all 3 nodes; sequentially restarted node1, then node2, then node3 via native `reboot`, polling each until reachable again and confirming its boot_id changed

Enabled mariadb at boot on all three nodes (was start-only before); after each restart the node auto-rejoined or was rejoined manually (node1's first reboot required a manual enable --now since it wasn't yet boot-enabled), quorum (2 remaining members, Synced) was preserved during each single-node outage
Verified final state: cluster size 3, all nodes wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced, appdb.orders contains all 4 committed rows (3 original + 1 post-maintenance write) identically on node1/node2/node3

evidence.requirement: Healthy 3-member Galera cluster established with application data
evidence.summary: Cluster bootstrapped on node1, node2 and node3 joined via SST reaching wsrep_cluster_size=3 and Synced on all members; appdb.orders table created with 3 committed rows and confirmed identical on node1, node2, and node3.

evidence.requirement: Full cluster shutdown for maintenance window
evidence.summary: mariadb stopped in order on node3, node2, node1 (node1 retaining safe_to_bootstrap:1 with highest seqno 17); systemctl is-active/ps confirmed all three nodes fully inactive with no mariadbd process.

evidence.requirement: Cluster brought back with every committed write present and all three members serving
evidence.summary: node1 bootstrapped and showed original 3 rows intact; node2 and node3 restarted and rejoined reaching cluster size 3 all Synced; a new write from node2 (post-maintenance-check) replicated correctly to node1 and node3, proving all three members serve reads and writes with data consistent.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id be303eb3-... captured; native `reboot` issued; quorum preserved on node2 (size 2, Synced) during outage; post-reboot boot_id changed to 2872ca6c-...; mariadb enabled and started, cluster size returned to 3 Synced with all appdb.orders rows intact.

evidence.requirement: node2 mandatory restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 21de1f79-... captured; native `reboot` issued; post-reboot boot_id changed to 1d6ba119-...; mariadb (now boot-enabled) auto-started and rejoined, cluster size 3 Synced with all data present.

evidence.requirement: node3 mandatory restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 8f258838-... captured; native `reboot` issued; post-reboot boot_id changed to 218bb58b-...; mariadb auto-started and rejoined, cluster size 3 Synced with all data present.

evidence.requirement: Final full-cluster health and data verification after all restarts
evidence.summary: node1 shows wsrep_cluster_size=3, Synced, wsrep_incoming_addresses lists all three node IPs, and appdb.orders COUNT(*)=4, matching the expected committed data set after the full restart cycle.
